units.content: Adaptive Intelligence Theory — Minimal Formal Skeleton (v0.1).
Intelligence is defined as expansion of controllable reachability through improved representations while preserving causal access required for continued correction and adaptation.
Adaptive Intelligence Genome: R_t -> Omega_t -> C_t -> A_t -> R_{t+1}.
R denotes representation quality.
Omega denotes controllable reachability.
C denotes correction capacity, glossed as reality's causal access.
A denotes adaptation capacity, glossed as improvement of generators.
dR/dt = f_R(A,C).
dOmega/dt = f_Omega(R,I).
dC/dt = f_C(Omega,R_e).
dA/dt = f_A(C,E).
I denotes interface / computational leverage.
R_e denotes strength of reality coupling.
E denotes evolvability mechanisms.
Stability constraint: Delta Omega_t <= C_t.
Alternative rate form: dOmega/dt <= kappa C_t.
Reachability expansion is stated to remain bounded by the system's ability to receive and incorporate corrective information from reality.
Reachability Expansion Ratio Gamma_t=(dOmega/dt)/C_t.
Gamma<1 is interpreted as expansion remaining within the correction envelope.
Gamma approximately 1 is interpreted as approaching the stability boundary.
Gamma>1 is interpreted as reachability growing faster than correction capacity.
Representation layer asks what structure the system can extract from reality.
Representation is stated to determine visible distinctions, compression ability, prediction quality, and possible interventions.
Representation layer names Representation Elasticity, Adaptive Metric Compiler, and Resolution Horizon as related frameworks; endpoints are unresolved here.
Reachability layer asks what futures the system can reliably influence.
Reachability is restricted to controllable futures under constraints rather than all imaginable futures.
Reachability layer names Causal Mass, Counterfactual Reachability Mass, and Interface-Induced Computational Geometry as related frameworks/concepts; exact endpoints unresolved.
Correction layer asks whether reality can still modify the system's trajectory.
Examples of correction channels: evolution selection/ecological feedback, science experiments/criticism, markets prices/failure, AI evaluation/feedback/corrigibility.
Correction layer names Causal Permeability, Alignment Spine, and CGET as related frameworks; exact endpoints unresolved.
Adaptation layer asks whether the system can improve mechanisms that produce future improvements.
Source distinguishes learning as changing current state from adaptation as changing the process generating future states.
Adaptation layer names Recursive Adaptive Dynamics and Adaptive Evolutionary Dynamics as related frameworks; exact endpoints unresolved.
Reachability runaway condition: dOmega/dt > C.
Reachability runaway is interpreted as influence increasing faster than corrective feedback.
Representation failure condition: R decreases.
Representation failure is interpreted as optimization using an inaccurate model.
Adaptation decoupling condition: A increases while C decreases, under PAGE_00 local meanings A=adaptation capacity and C=correction capacity.
Adaptation decoupling is interpreted as self-improvement while losing connection to reality.
Stagnation condition: C increases while A decreases, under PAGE_00 local meanings.
Stagnation is interpreted as stability without ability to improve.
How can systems increase their ability to transform reality without losing their ability to learn from reality?

Minimal experimental program proposes independently controlling representation quality R, reachable action space Omega, feedback fidelity/delay C, and self-modification capacity A in changing environments.
Primary prediction: sustainable intelligence growth requires dOmega/dt <= kappa C.
Theory predicts intelligence growth is constrained by maintaining coupling between increasing power and continued correction, not by capability alone.
Adaptive Intelligence Theory (AIT).
How can a system expand its ability to influence the future while preserving conditions required for continued improvement?
AIT views intelligence as adaptive dynamics rather than static capability; central object is improvement of models/actions and corrigibility under changing conditions, not performance alone.
Adaptive loop diagram: Reality -> Observation -> Representation -> Compression -> Prediction/Search -> Action -> Reality Change -> Feedback -> loop.
Formal loop: R_t -> M_t -> A_t -> E_{t+1} -> R_{t+1}.
In PAGE_1 loop, R_t denotes representation of reality.
In PAGE_1 loop, M_t denotes internal model and search process.
In PAGE_1 adaptive-loop context, A_t denotes action.
In PAGE_1 adaptive-loop context, E_t denotes environment.
Intelligence is stated to be capacity to improve the adaptive loop over time.
Possibility-space section defines Omega as the set of possible future states.
Capability expansion is represented as Delta Omega > 0.
Increasing capability is stated to expand both best achievable and worst achievable futures.
Proposed directed-expansion objective: Delta Omega_good > Delta Omega_bad.
In PAGE_1 Alignment Principle context, A_t is redefined as alignment (or correction) capacity.
In PAGE_1 Alignment Principle context, C_t denotes capability.
Adaptive stability condition proposed as A_t >= C_t under PAGE_1 alignment/capability meanings.
Instability regime proposed when C_t > A_t under PAGE_1 alignment/capability meanings.
Capability without proportional correction is stated to produce increasing instability because change production exceeds error detection/correction.
Optimization is stated to be fundamentally limited by representation; reliable optimization requires adequate representation.
Higher-quality representations are stated to expand controllable futures through prediction, search, abstraction, and intervention.
Proposed adaptive objective recursively improves representation of reality, ability to act, and ability to detect/correct errors.
Proposed adaptive objective preserves contact with reality, reliable feedback, and alignment with beneficial futures.
Recursive improvement without correction is stated to eventually diverge.
Correction without improvement is stated to eventually stagnate; sustained intelligence requires both.
Central thesis: intelligence is ability to improve processes that discover, evaluate, and create answers while remaining corrigible under changing reality, not merely ability to find answers.
